audits.title: A prospective audit of adherence to safe sleeping guidelines in a general paediatric ward and special care nursery.
audits.standard: 10 safe sleeping compliance rules based on national and international guidelines
audits.setting: Special care nursery and general paediatric ward, Canberra Hospital

cycle1.result: Supine sleeping compliance 83% (SCN) and 82% (GPW); median compliance score 8 (IQR 7-9) in SCN versus 7 (IQR 6-7) in GPW.

audits.other_findings: The full set of safe sleeping guidelines was not implemented.

audits.title: The EASE Quality Improvement Project: Improving Safe Sleep Practices in Ohio Children's Hospitals.
audits.standard: American Academy of Pediatrics safe sleep recommendations
audits.setting: Six children's hospitals in Ohio; statewide QI programme

cycle1.result: 279 of 856 (32.6%) sleeping infants observed following AAP recommendations.

audits.intervention: Hospital safe sleep teams ran at least 3 PDSA cycles of multifactorial interventions over 12 months, with weekly audits.
audits.other_findings: 5343 audits collected in total; family report of safe sleep education also improved.
audits.citation: Macklin JR, Gittelman MA, Denny SA, Southworth H, Arnold MW. The EASE Quality Improvement Project: Improving Safe Sleep Practices in Ohio Children's Hospitals. Pediatrics. 2016;138(4):e20154267. doi:10.1542/peds.2015-4267. PMID: 27630074.

audits.title: Quality improvement initiative to improve infant safe sleep practices in the newborn nursery.
audits.standard: AAP Infant Safe Sleep guidelines; composite 'perfect sleep' measure; aim 70% within 1 year
audits.setting: Mother-baby unit, suburban community hospital in North Carolina (Duke University Health System)

cycle1.result: 41.9% of sleeping infants met 'perfect sleep'; 38.0% of sleep areas had extra items; 15.3% inappropriately bundled; 87.0% in a safe location; 90.3% on their back; 3.8% raised bassinette head.

audits.intervention: Seven PDSA cycles: nursing education module; parent education with door hangers then crib cards; temporary then permanent supply of wearable blankets (sleep sacks) with laundering; reminder to labour ward nurses to give empty bassinettes; gifting sleep sacks to take home.

cycle2.result: 'Perfect sleep' rose to 67.3% (goal of 70% not met); extra items 20.2%; inappropriate bundling 3.8%; safe location 92.0%; back sleeping 98.1%.

audits.other_findings: Improvements were sustained over 12 months after the last PDSA cycle; over 3100 observations were recorded in total. Extra items in the bassinette, often due to storage, remained the main cause of failure.
audits.citation: Shaikh SK, Chamberlain L, Nazareth-Pidgeon KM, Boggan JC. Quality improvement initiative to improve infant safe sleep practices in the newborn nursery. BMJ Open Qual. 2022;11(3):e001834. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2022-001834. PMID: 35922090.
